related_questions.question: Can I drive in Austria with a US license?

text_blocks.snippet: No, a U.S. driver's license alone is not sufficient to drive in Austria. You need either an International Driving Permit (IDP) or an official translation of your U.S. license. The IDP can be obtained in the U.S. from AAA. Alternatively, you can obtain a German translation of your U.S. license from Austrian automobile clubs, like ÖAMTC or ARBÖ.
snippet_highlighted_words: No, a U.S. driver's license alone is not sufficient to drive in Austria

list.title: IDP:
list.snippet: An International Driving Permit is a translation of your valid U.S. driver's license into multiple languages, including German.

list.title: Official Translation:
list.snippet: You can also obtain an official translation of your U.S. license from Austrian automobile clubs.

list.title: Rental Car:
list.snippet: When renting a car in Austria, you'll likely need to present both your U.S. driver's license and either the IDP or the official translation.

list.title: Tourists:
list.snippet: For tourists, an IDP is generally required in conjunction with your U.S. license.

list.title: Residents:
list.snippet: If you become a resident of Austria, you can only use your U.S. license for six months. After that, you must exchange it for an Austrian license.
